(2) Each pages differently: the two charts are ordered by different columns (`top`, `new`), and the category page also filters. (3) `catalog_page` is a **keyset** reader: it can say "the page after this cursor" and nothing else, so it cannot give page numbers, a total, or "page 7 of 40"; the migration's own comment says license, size and A-Z order are "not indexed, deliberately", so the category page's `license` and `maxSize` filters (done in memory today over the whole category) have **no database form** until a migration adds one. **The split.** `5.l.x.zi` (9a): one function in a new lib file, `readAppsPage({ scope, order, after, pageSize })`, that returns the first-party apps (from `getFirstPartyList`, once, on the first page only) followed by one `readCatalogPage` page of third-party rows (first-party package names dropped, as `catalog-shelf.ts` does), plus the cursor's place in the URL (`?after=<opaque cursor>`, reusing `encodeCursor`/`decodeCursor`; a bad cursor is a first page, not an error) and a `Pager` component ("Next page" as a plain link, so it works without JavaScript and is crawlable); no page uses it yet. `5.l.x.zo` (9b): `/charts/top-free` on it, order `top`, the two sections kept (first-party, then third-party). `5.l.xi.zi` (9c): `/charts/new` on it, order `new`. `5.l.xi.zo` (9d): `/apps`, every app and game, order `top`, paged, linked from the `/categories` index. `5.l.xii.zi` (9e): the category page on it for table mode, filters hidden in table mode. `5.l.xii.zo` (9f): `p_license` and `p_max_size_mb` added to `catalog_page` (new migration, the operator applies it) and the filters wired back. **Decisions, for the operator to overrule:** (a) **"Next page" only, no page numbers and no totals**, because the reader is keyset; going back is the browser's back button. The alternative is an offset reader, which gets slow deep into 10,000 rows and drifts when rows change, so it is not proposed. (b) **Rank numbers on Top Free**: a keyset page cannot know how many rows came before it, so the first cut carries the rank offset in the URL (`?n=<count so far>`, clamped, display only, never used to read data) so page 2 starts at 25, not 1. If the operator would rather have no ranks after page 1, say so in 9b. (c) **First-party apps appear on page 1 only** and are never repeated, in every list. (f) The `/categories` index's counts (`getTaxonomyAppCount`, `getCategoryAppCount`) also read the whole merged catalog; they are **not** in 9a to 9f and are left for `5.l.vii.zi` (cleanup) to find, because a count per category from the database is its own query and its own migration. (g) `5.l.v.zo` (search) is untouched and will reuse 9a. **Current position moves to `5.l.x.zi`.** Leaf 6 (`5.l.iii.zo`) is still the operator's, and so is the re-derive (`--dry-run`, then the real run) that makes category pages show anything. > **Resolved (2026-10-02, out-of-band follow-up to the note below, roadmap position unchanged; not a leaf, count stays `22 done ✅ of 41`) — (1) a site-wide fluid-layout safety net, (2) the home hero's View button moved to the right and made transparent.** (1) Operator: make the layout fit every device so the overflow cannot come back on any page. Read from the whole CSS tree, not run: `app/globals.css` gains a block of zero-specificity defaults (`:where()`): `text-size-adjust: 100%`; `max-width: 100%` on `img, video, svg, canvas, iframe, embed, object, picture`; `overflow-wrap: anywhere` on the text elements (`p, li, dd, dt, h1`-`h6, blockquote, figcaption, summary, legend, caption, label, code, kbd, samp`; inherited, so inline links and chips inside them wrap, and `anywhere` also lets flex and grid items shrink; buttons and form controls are left out on purpose); `pre` scrolls inside its own box; and everything directly inside a page's `<main>` gets `min-width: 0; max-width: 100%` (all 32 pages render their own `<main>`). `components/Footer.module.css` lost its two `white-space: nowrap` lines (a long copyright or totals line widened the page on a narrow phone). The remaining `nowrap` rules were each read and left: screen-reader-only text, small badges and counts, ellipsised names, and the category bar's chips (inside its own horizontal scroller). Together with `minimumScale: 1` in `app/layout.tsx` this is belt and braces: the rules stop the overflow, the viewport stops the zoom-out if something new slips through. **Admin pages were not audited** (`app/admin/*` has two `min-width: 160px` filters, not touched). (2) `components/Hero.tsx`: the button is no longer inside the text column (it took a whole row under the summary); it is a direct child of the card's panel, at the right edge, labelled "View" (accessible name "View <app name>"). `components/Hero.module.css`: no fill, a 1.5px outline and label in `--color-accent`, hover and press are 14% and 26% tints of that accent, so it follows the dark and light tokens and a category's contextual skin with no colour of its own; on a card narrower than icon + text + button (560px and below) the button wraps under the text and stays right-aligned. `SkeletonHero` mirrors it (button placeholder moved to the right). **Not verified in a browser** (no testing, standing instruction). **Decisions, for the operator to overrule:** the label is "View" (was "View app"); the outline is 60% accent at rest.

> **Resolved (2026-10-02, out-of-band fix, roadmap position unchanged; not a leaf, so the count stays `22 done ✅ of 41`) — the app detail page was not responsive on a phone: the page rendered zoomed out with a blank band down one side (operator screenshot of an Aptoide app, the permissions list visible).** Cause, read from the code, not run: the permission chips (`components/PermissionsDisclosure.module.css`, and `DataSafety.module.css`, which copied it) are `inline-block` boxes with no break rule, and one permission name such as `com.google.android.finsky.permission.BIND_GET_INSTALL_REFERRER_SERVICE` is about 70 characters, wider than a phone's content column, so the chip overflowed the page. The global `overflow-x: clip` hides the overflow but a mobile browser still zoomed the whole page out to fit it, which is the tiny text and the empty band. **Fix:** (1) both chips now wrap inside their own box (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`, `max-width: 100%`, `min-width: 0` on the flex item); (2) the same rule on the app description paragraphs and list (`ExpandableDescription.module.css`) and the release notes (`Changelog.module.css`), where a long URL would do the same; (3) `app/layout.tsx`'s `viewport` export now says `width: device-width`, `initialScale: 1`, `minimumScale: 1`, so a mobile browser may not zoom the page out below 1 even if some future element overflows (zooming in is still allowed). **Not verified in a browser** (no testing, standing instruction): the operator should open an app with a long permission list on the phone after deploy. **Decision, for the operator to overrule:** `minimumScale: 1` is a safety net that hides future overflow bugs rather than showing them as a zoomed-out page; remove it from `app/layout.tsx` if overflow should stay visible while developing. **Not checked:** other pages for the same pattern (a long unbroken token in an inline-block); only the detail page's own sections were read.

## 1. The Rule, stated plainly

**Every session does exactly one leaf task. No more, no less.**

- Do not start a second leaf even if time/context remains — end the session, hand off, let the next session pick up `zo` or the next milestone.
- Do not leave a leaf half-done. If a leaf turns out to be bigger than one session, stop and split it into a new sub-leaf pair before writing any code, then hand off the split itself as the session's one task.
- Always re-read "Current position" before doing anything else.

---

## 2. Full Task Hierarchy

### Phase 0 — UI Revamp (PRIORITY — supersedes prior sequencing until complete)

*Added by resequencing. Full storefront UI, live-previewable on Vercel, running entirely on dummy/mock data seeded from the apps currently in the catalog — no real backend calls (no Supabase, no Telegram, no Doctrine) at this stage. Every data-dependent interaction (install button, ratings, search, filters, report form) uses local dummy logic so the whole app is clickable and visually complete. This becomes the working roadmap/reference for what the real backend (Phase 5 infra, Supabase, etc.) needs to eventually support underneath. Once Phase 0 is complete, sequencing resumes at `5.f.i.zi` (provision Supabase) so real data gets wired in behind the same interfaces established here.*

Distinct from `0.b.iii.zi`'s no-flash-on-load guarantee — this smooths the swap once a visitor actually toggles, via the future `0.c.i.zo` control

**0.h — Geo-Regionalization Foundation** *(new — see "Scope addition" note above. The one Phase 0 track allowed a real external call; everything catalog-side still runs on dummy data.)*
- 0.h.i — IP geolocation client (ipapi.co)
  - [x] 0.h.i.zi — Global `ipapi.co` client wrapper (typed response, timeout, graceful fallback to a default region on error/429/rate-limit — never blocks rendering) — `lib/ipapi.ts`, `lookupRegion()`. Scope deliberately narrow: just the client. Hits `https://ipapi.co/json/` with a 2.5s `AbortController` timeout; treats both a non-2xx status *and* ipapi.co's own in-body `{ error: true }` shape (their free tier returns HTTP 200 with an error body for some failure modes, not only a 4xx/5xx status) as failures; any of those, a timeout, or a network/parse error all fall back the same way to a fixed `DEFAULT_REGION` (`US`) rather than throwing or returning `null` — callers never have to special-case a missing result. No caching/session-dedup (0.h.i.zo, next), no React context or cookie wiring (same leaf), no catalog coupling (`available_regions` doesn't exist yet, 0.h.ii.zi) — all explicitly out of scope here per the `0.h` heading note. `next build` passes clean; manually verified the actual fallback path (not just reasoned about it) by running `lookupRegion()` standalone via `npx tsx` — this sandbox's own network egress doesn't allowlist `ipapi.co`, so the real fetch fails immediately, and it correctly resolved `{ country_code: "US", country_name: "United States", source: "default" }` in 83ms without throwing.
  - [x] 0.h.i.zo — Region-context provider: calls the client (`0.h.i.zi`) once per visitor session (cached — cookie or edge cache, not per-request), exposes detected country/region to the component tree; no catalog coupling yet — closes out `0.h.i`. Split three ways: `middleware.ts` is the write side — the only place that can both read an incoming request's cookies and set one on the response before any page renders, so it's what makes "once per session" real: if `d-store-region` is already present it's a no-op passthrough, otherwise it calls `lookupRegion()` and sets the cookie, with no `maxAge`/`expires` (a true session cookie, not a long-lived preference like the theme cookie). `lib/region.ts` is the read side, mirroring `lib/theme.ts`'s cookie-read-in-a-server-component shape (`getRegion()`, called from `app/layout.tsx`) — decodes the JSON cookie value, falls back to the same `US` default `lib/ipapi.ts` uses if the cookie is somehow missing or malformed. `components/RegionProvider.tsx` is the component-tree side — a thin client-only React context (required because context needs a client boundary) seeded server-side via the `region` prop from layout, no client-side fetching at all, same no-flash reasoning the theme cookie already uses. `useRegion()` has no consumers yet, same as `available_regions` not existing yet — both wait for `0.h.ii`. `next build` passes clean (middleware compiles into its own bundle, 34.7 kB); manually verified end-to-end via `next start`: first request sets `Set-Cookie: d-store-region=...` with the fallback region (`ipapi.co` isn't in this sandbox's network allowlist, so this also incidentally re-proves 0.h.i.zi's fallback path under real middleware conditions, not just standalone), a second request sent with that cookie gets no `Set-Cookie` at all (cache hit, lookup genuinely skipped), and `/`, `/app/f-droid`, `/developer/fdroid` all still render 200 with the provider wrapping the tree.
- 0.h.ii — Region-aware dummy catalog scaffold
  - [x] 0.h.ii.zi — Extend `lib/mock-data.ts` `App` shape with a dummy `available_regions: string[]` field (still 100% local dummy data — no live catalog calls) — plus a new `ALL_REGIONS` const (9 ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, a representative set of large markets, not all ~195 countries — this is Phase 0 scaffolding). Unlike most §7-era fields, this one has no real-world basis to seed from: FOSS Android apps are essentially never region-locked, so there's no legacy-entity or screenshot source of truth to transcribe the way `license`/`source`/etc. were. It exists purely so `0.h.ii.zo`'s region-filter helper has something to narrow against. 8 of the 13 apps carry `[...ALL_REGIONS]` (the honest default); 5 carry a deliberately narrower dummy subset (`battery-live`, `night-mode-enabler`, `awesomewallpaper`, `enhancement`, `greyscale`) so the filter has a non-trivial case to prove it actually filters, not just a no-op over an always-everywhere catalog. Every app includes `"US"` on purpose — matches `lib/ipapi.ts`'s `DEFAULT_REGION`, so a visitor whose geolocation lookup fell back to the default never gets filtered out of the whole catalog. `lib/catalog.ts` deliberately untouched this leaf — no fetch function consumes the field yet, per the leaf's own "no live catalog calls" scope; that wiring is `0.h.ii.zo`, next. `next build` passes clean — every app literal satisfying the now-required `available_regions` field is itself a type-level integrity check (a missing field on any of the 13 would have failed the build); additionally verified via a standalone script that all 13 apps have a non-empty list, every code used falls inside `ALL_REGIONS`, and all 13 include `"US"`.
  - [x] 0.h.ii.zo — Region-filter helper in the dummy data-fetch layer (`0.a.ii.zo`) that narrows `apps` by the detected region — the seam future Play-Store-style regionalized queries plug into once Supabase (`5.f.i`) lands. Closes out `0.h` and **Phase 0 in its entirety**. `lib/catalog.ts` gains `filterAppsByRegion(source, regionCode)` — a standalone exported pure filter over `App.available_regions` (`0.h.ii.zi`) — plus a `region?: string` option on `GetAppsOptions`, wired into `getApps()` alongside the existing `category`/`license`/`maxSizeMb` filters, composable with all three the same sequential-`.filter()` way `0.g.ii.zo` added `license`/`maxSizeMb`. Deliberately the *only* fetch function this leaf wires `region` into — `0.h` is a "Foundation," not a "Feature" (per its own heading note and the "Scope addition" note above): threading region through every shelf/search/similar-apps function on dummy data now would be scope creep for a leaf whose actual job is handing the real backend work (once Supabase lands) a seam to plug into, not turning on region filtering everywhere today. Nothing calls `getApps({ region: ... })` from any page yet — same "helper exists, not yet consumed" shape `getDeveloperBySlug`/`getAppsByDeveloper` had for one commit before `0.g.iii.zo` wired them up. `next build` passes clean; manually verified end-to-end via a standalone script calling the real `getApps()`: unfiltered returns all 13; `region: "IN"` correctly returns the 9 apps that include it (8 `ALL_REGIONS` apps + `battery-live`, which was given a narrower `["US","GB","IN"]` list in `0.h.ii.zi` specifically to be a non-trivial case); `region: "JP"` similarly returns the 9 that include it (8 `ALL_REGIONS` + `awesomewallpaper`); a bogus code (`"ZZ"`) correctly returns zero rather than silently matching everything; and `{ category: "theming", region: "DE" }` composes correctly with the existing category filter.

"Sanctuary" dark also passed cleanly (`accent` 10.74:1/9.74:1, `accentStrong` 8.05:1/7.30:1), and light `accentStrong` passed (5.78:1/6.11:1) — but light `accent` (`#5b7fbd`) did not: 3.64:1/3.84:1, clearing only the 3:1 large-text/UI-component threshold, not the 4.5:1 normal-text bar that applies here since `--color-accent` is used as ordinary-size `color` across this repo's components (`Header`, `Footer`, `Hero`, `AppCard`, `RatingSummary`, etc.), not just large text or isolated UI chrome — a real AA failure, not a false alarm from applying the wrong threshold. **Phase 0 — UI Revamp is complete, plus the `0.i` extension above.** Every leaf across `0.a`–`0.h` is checked off; `0.i` (Category-Adaptive Theming) is new scope layered on top per the "Priority override" note and takes precedence over continuing further down the roadmap — see Current position. Once `0.i` is done, the next leaf per docs/D-STORE.md's roadmap is `1.a.i.zo` (Phase 1 — Foundation, Data Model Migration), picking up where the Phase 0 detour began — `5.f.i.zi` (provision Supabase) is still the first *real backend* leaf and remains gated behind Phase 1–4 per the existing roadmap ordering; neither Phase 0 nor `0.i` landing changes that sequencing, it just means the UI this real backend will eventually sit behind is more fully scaffolded.

Per D-STORE.md §4.C — "Scroll-triggered reveal, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`" is one requirement, not two — `prefers-reduced-motion` is checked directly in this leaf (both in the hook, which returns already-revealed with no observer for a reduced-motion visitor, and as a CSS backstop for the gap before that effect runs), not deferred to the later `3.d.iii` reduced-motion audit.   - [x] 3.c.iii.zi — Report-flag queue UI *(Unheld 2026-09-30 — decision recorded below. **Ticked 2026-10-01, verification session:** the marker was a stale parent; all three parts are done and ticked as items 14a to 14c7 of focus run 2.)*
      - WIP — **only the first of three parts is done.** The Section 1 split this leaf required was never recorded. Part 1, report intake write route (`POST /api/apps/[slug]/reports`, commit `248cea2`, rebuilt in the 2026-10-01 fix session — see `5.d.ii.zo`'s note), is done. **Still open:** part 2, per-moderator authentication (split, now done except as noted); part 3, the queue UI (split on 2026-10-01 into 14c1–14c7). They are items 14b and 14c in the focus run 2 checklist.
      - Split of part 2, 2026-10-01 (docs-only, no code changed): **per-moderator authentication was more than one session** and a read of the repo turned up two problems that change where it goes. Read, not run: `middleware.ts`, `lib/admin-auth.ts`, `app/api/apps/[slug]/reports/route.ts`, `lib/rate-limit.ts`, the `report_flag` and `application` migrations, `docs/MODERATION.md`; Zealot and Storeapp were not cloned, nothing here touches either. **Findings:** (a) **The report intake route cannot save a report for a real catalog app.** It resolves the slug through `public.application` (`GET /rest/v1/application?slug=eq.…`) and answers `404` when no row exists, but nothing in the repo ever inserts into `application` (a grep over `app/`, `lib/`, `scripts/`, `.github/` and the migrations finds only its own `alter`s and two foreign keys), and the counters migration (`20260930100000`) already says the catalog lives in Zealot's index and Aptoide, so `application` is not where a slug is guaranteed to exist. Unless someone inserts rows by hand, every report is answered `404`; part 1's tick (14a) stays `[x]` because the route does what its text said, but it is **flagged**, and nothing about a queue is useful until it is fixed (14b3, 14b4). `report_flag.application_id` is `not null` and a foreign key, so the fix is a migration, not only a route edit. (b) **The queue cannot live under `/admin`.** `middleware.ts` sends every `/admin/*` and `/api/admin/*` request through the shared-password check first, so a moderator would need the shared password before their own sign-in is even read, which defeats "individually, not through the shared admin password" (Question 2, option A). The queue therefore lives at a new prefix, **`/moderation` and `/api/moderation`**, outside `isAdminPath`, with its own gate; the shared `ADMIN_PASSWORD` never opens it and a moderator token never opens `/admin`. (c) **What "individual" means here, decided on industry-standard practice and recorded so it can be overruled:** each moderator has a **generated token, not a chosen password**, sent as the Basic-auth password with the moderator's id as the username (D-Store has no accounts, `3.c.iv.zi`; Supabase Auth and an OAuth login were considered and rejected: no live Supabase project exists, either one adds sessions, callbacks and a store of staff personal data, and neither is needed for a handful of people). Config is one server-only env var, **`MODERATOR_TOKENS`**, a JSON array of `{ "id", "sha256" }` where `sha256` is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the token, so the secret itself is never in Vercel's env; `id` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{1,31}$`; at most 20 entries; a duplicate id, a malformed entry or unparseable JSON makes the **whole** config invalid, which **fails closed** (`503` to everyone, never open), as `ADMIN_PASSWORD` unset does. A token is at least 32 characters, no whitespace, generated (`openssl rand -base64 24` gives 32), so a fast hash is the right one; **if a human is ever allowed to pick a password this decision must change** to a slow hash. Verification uses Web Crypto only (SHA-256 and a byte-wise compare, like `lib/admin-auth.ts`) so the same function runs in the Edge middleware; an unknown id and a wrong token take the same path (the stored digest is replaced by a dummy, the compare still runs) and both answer `401`. The result of a good check carries the moderator's id, so a later leaf can record who decided. Revoking a moderator is deleting their entry. Same three layers as the admin gate (middleware, a guard at the top of every `/api/moderation` handler, a guard at the top of every `/moderation` page), the same `Origin` check on `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE`, `Cache-Control: no-store` and `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`. (4) Extra keys on an entry (a `"note"`) are **ignored**, not rejected, so an operator can label an entry. (4) `ScreenshotCarousel.module.css`'s `scroll-behavior: smooth` is correctly left ungated too, per that file's own existing comment — it only affects programmatic scrolls, and none exist yet (plain server component, no scroll-to call site). (5) **Real gap, fixed:** `app/admin/featuring/page.module.css`'s `.toggleKnob` had an ungated `transition: transform 0.15s ease` — the one transform-transition in the whole codebase that didn't follow the `3.a.ii.zi` convention, missed because the admin surface's own focus-visible gap (`3.d.i.zo`) was audited from the *keyboard-nav* angle, not the motion angle. Moved the transition into a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` block around `.toggleKnob`, same shape as `StickyInstallBar.module.css`'s `.bar`; a reduced-motion visitor now gets the toggle's on/off position change with no animated slide, same as everywhere else in the repo. Verified in the compiled CSS output: `.toggleKnob`'s `transition` now sits inside the media-query rule, not the base rule. No JS-driven motion (`requestAnimationFrame`/`setInterval`) exists anywhere in the codebase to audit separately — `useScrollReveal.ts` is the one place JS checks `matchMedia(\"(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)\")` directly, already correct. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `next build` both pass clean.
  - [x] 3.d.iii.zo — Static fallback states for all animations — Done, audit only, no code changes needed: checked every animation found by `3.d.iii.zi` for what a `reduce`-motion visitor actually sees once the animation is skipped, not just that it's skipped. (1) The five `@keyframes` components (`Hero`, `InstallButton`, `Lightbox`, `Skeleton`, `WavyProgressRing`): in every case the `animation` property itself sits entirely inside the `no-preference` block, so a `reduce` visitor never applies it at all and simply renders each element's own un-animated base styles — confirmed none of those base styles are hidden/zero-opacity/mid-transform (`Hero`'s `.panel`/`.icon` have no `opacity`/`transform` outside the keyframes; `Lightbox`'s `.dialog`/`::backdrop` render fully opaque with no base transform; `Skeleton`'s `.shimmer` is a plain solid `--color-border` block, still legibly "loading" without the sweep). No fallback is "frozen mid-animation" anywhere. (2) `InstallButton`'s progress `.fill` and `WavyProgressRing`'s `.ring` go further and explicitly `display: none` under `reduce` rather than relying on the implicit base state, specifically because their base state (`width: 0%` / `stroke-dashoffset: 100`, i.e. permanently "0% progress") would otherwise read as a broken, stuck-at-zero indicator, not a neutral absence of one — checked that this doesn't leave the "installing" state illegible without them: `InstallButton.tsx`'s `[data-state="installing"]` button carries its own distinct background/dim styling (`InstallButton.module.css`) plus an "Installing…"/"Updating…" text label, `disabled` state, and `aria-live="polite"`/`aria-label` announcement — all independent of the fill bar, so the fallback communicates progress state through text and disabled-styling rather than motion, not through nothing at all. (3) `ScrollReveal` is the one component whose *base* (non-media-query) state is genuinely hidden (`opacity: 0`, since visibility is driven by an `IntersectionObserver` via a `.revealed` class, not by animation timing) — already correctly backstopped two ways: an explicit `@media (reduce) { .reveal { opacity: 1; transform: none } }` CSS rule, and `useScrollReveal.ts`'s own `matchMedia` check that sets `isRevealed` immediately for a `reduce` visitor, covering the gap between first paint and that effect running (per that hook's own header comment, this was deliberately built into `3.a.i.zi` rather than deferred to this audit). (4) `StickyInstallBar.module.css`'s `.bar` also starts `opacity: 0`/`visibility: hidden` outside any media query, but that's `data-visible`-driven show/hide logic (an `IntersectionObserver` watching the header), not animation-timing-driven — orthogonal to `prefers-reduced-motion`, which only strips the `.bar`'s `transition` (confirmed already present, `reduce` block sets `transition: none`), so the show/hide itself still functions correctly, just instantly. (5) Every transform-based `:active` press effect (`3.d.iii.zi`'s finding 2) has no separate "fallback" to design: removing the whole rule under `reduce` correctly returns the element to its plain resting style, which is a complete, non-broken state on its own — WCAG 2.3.3 requires interaction-triggered motion be disable-able, not replaced with a substitute non-motion cue, so no gap here. Grepped the full codebase for `requestAnimationFrame`/`setInterval`-driven visual state (none exist) and every base `opacity: 0`/hidden declaration sitewide (7 occurrences, all covered by the reasoning above) to make sure this audit wasn't just re-checking the `no-preference` gating `3.d.iii.zi` already confirmed. Closes out `3.d.iii` (Reduced motion) and, with it, all of `3.d` (Accessibility & Performance) and Phase 3 (Motion, Metrics & Charts) — `3.c.iii.zi`/`zo` remain open but Held (Zealot ❓6, unrelated to this track). `npx tsc --noEmit` and `next build` both pass clean (no files changed by this leaf).

  - [x] 4.b.i.zi — Web app manifest — `app/manifest.ts` (Next's App Router manifest-file convention, served at `/manifest.webmanifest` and auto-linked from `<head>`, no manual `<link rel="manifest">` needed) plus `public/icon.svg` (new, this leaf's only image asset — a static, hand-authored brand mark reusing `AppIcon.tsx`'s gradient+glyph+gloss convention but with dark theme's token *values* hardcoded, since a manifest icon has no CSS-variable runtime; one SVG covers both `"any"` and `"maskable"` purpose entries). `id`/`start_url: "/"`/`display: "standalone"` are the fields that actually make the browser's install prompt available; `background_color`/`theme_color` reuse dark theme's own `--color-bg` (`#0a0908`) since no per-theme manifest variant exists yet (`4.b.ii`, "Theme-aware app icons," is the next milestone and where that gets addressed, not this leaf). `app/layout.tsx` gained a `viewport` export with the matching `themeColor` — Next 15 moved that key out of the `metadata` export into its own `viewport` export, so this keeps the deprecated-field warning from firing while staying the single place both the `<meta name="theme-color">` tag and the manifest's own `theme_color` are sourced from. `next build` passes clean (`/manifest.webmanifest` compiles as a static `○` route, same as `/sitemap.xml`); manually verified via `next start` that `/manifest.webmanifest` (200, well-formed JSON with the expected fields) and `/icon.svg` (200) both serve correctly, and that the rendered `/` head contains both `<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest"/>` and `<meta name="theme-color" content="#0a0908"/>`.
  - [x] 4.b.i.zo — Service worker offline shell — `public/sw.js` (plain vanilla worker, no Workbox/next-pwa dependency added, matching this repo's native-platform-API preference) plus `components/ServiceWorkerRegister.tsx` (registers it on mount, mounted from `app/layout.tsx` next to `Header`/`Footer` so it's active on every page) and the fallback route it serves, `app/offline/page.tsx` + `page.module.css` (copies the privacy/terms prose shell). Deliberately narrow scope, not full offline catalog browsing: every page here is server-rendered per request (theme/region cookies, `lib/catalog.ts`'s runtime catalog read), so there's no static page HTML this worker could correctly cache offline — instead it (1) tries the network first for any navigation and falls back to the precached `/offline` page only on failure, and (2) opportunistically cache-first's same-origin `/_next/static/*` requests, since those filenames are content-hashed and safe to cache indefinitely once fetched. API routes, `/manifest.webmanifest`, and everything cross-origin pass through untouched — no risk of serving stale dynamic data to an online visitor. `next build` passes clean (`/offline` a new `ƒ` route); manually verified via `next start` that `/offline` and `/sw.js` both return 200, `/sw.js` is served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0` (so browsers revalidate it promptly rather than caching a stale worker), and `/offline`'s body renders the expected "You're offline" copy.

  - [x] 4.b.ii.zi — Theme-aware app icons — `public/icon-light.svg` (new), a hand-authored light-theme variant of `4.b.i.zi`'s `public/icon.svg`, built from light theme's own token *values* (`--color-bg #f7f8fa`, `--color-accent #2454c9`, `--color-accent-strong #1a3d99`) rather than a brightness-inverted copy of the dark icon — same "must genuinely diverge" rule `0.i`/`0.b.iv` already established for theme-adjacent assets; the background gradient leans on the same cool-cobalt-glow shape `0.b.iv.zo`'s light `--gradient-vignette` introduced, and the gloss highlight uses a low-opacity accent tint instead of dark theme's white highlight, since a white highlight would be invisible against this near-white base. `app/manifest.ts` made async and now calls `getTheme()` (`lib/theme.ts`, 0.b.iii.zi) — the same theme-cookie read `app/layout.tsx` already does for `data-theme` — to resolve `icons[].src`/`background_color`/`theme_color` per visitor instead of always returning dark theme's values; this opts the route out of static generation (expected for a now-cookie-dependent response). `next build` passes clean; manually verified via `next start` that `/manifest.webmanifest` returns dark theme's `/icon.svg` + `#0a0908`/`#0a0908` with no cookie and light theme's `/icon-light.svg` + `#f7f8fa`/`#2454c9` with an explicit `Cookie: d-store-theme=light` header, and that both `/icon.svg` and `/icon-light.svg` serve 200.
  - [x] 4.b.ii.zo — Splash screens per theme — `public/splash.svg` (dark) and `public/splash-light.svg` (light, both new), reusing `icon.svg`/`icon-light.svg`'s gradient-background + "D"-glyph construction at a representative portrait-phone aspect ratio (1170×2532) rather than a per-device raster pipeline — a splash is a plain background wash plus a centered wordmark, with no fine detail that needs exact pixel-for-pixel matching per device, so one scalable vector asset per theme covers every breakpoint honestly. `app/layout.tsx`'s static `metadata` export replaced with `generateMetadata()` (same async, cookie-reading pattern `4.b.ii.zi` already gave `app/manifest.ts`) so `appleWebApp.startupImage` resolves the correct theme's splash per visitor; `appleWebApp.capable: true` is included because it's the flag that makes iOS treat the site as standalone at all — without it none of the `startupImage` entries would ever show, so it's necessary to this leaf's feature rather than scope creep, and `statusBarStyle` (`black-translucent` dark / `default` light) is included for the same "does the launch experience look right" reason `theme_color` already varies per theme in the manifest. `startupImage`'s four `media` breakpoints are a representative subset of Apple's own much longer device-splash list (one compact-phone, one standard-phone, one large-phone, one tablet class) — same "representative, not exhaustive" scope this repo already applies elsewhere (e.g. `5.h`'s curated Aptoide category set); a model outside those four still gets a correctly themed, correctly proportioned splash from the nearest breakpoint's vector asset, just not pixel-matched to that exact device's native resolution. iOS only shows a splash for a standalone-mode site and only reads it from these `<link rel="apple-touch-startup-image">` tags — it does not derive one from the web manifest the way Android/Chrome does, so this is genuinely separate work from `4.b.ii.zi`'s manifest changes, not a duplicate of them. `next build` passes clean; manually verified via `next start` that `/` (no cookie) renders all four `apple-touch-startup-image` links pointed at `/splash.svg` plus `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style: black-translucent`, that an explicit `Cookie: d-store-theme=light` header swaps all four to `/splash-light.svg` plus `status-bar-style: default`, and that both `/splash.svg` and `/splash-light.svg` serve 200.

So the work is (1) a data shape and a reader that survives hostile input, (2) filling it in the normalizer, (3) a display component, (4) mounting it on a page with a first-party and a third-party state — verified as a pure unit test, a fabricated-index run, a render, and a `next start` pass. **Findings that shaped the split, read from the repo and not assumed:** (a) `RawVersion` has **no date**: it carries `release_id`, `version_name`, `download_url`, `sha256`, `size_bytes`, `signing_fingerprint`, `changelog`, `compatibility.min_sdk` and the optional `rollout`, so a per-version release date cannot be shown and must not be invented from `updated_at` (that is the app's, not the version's); (b) the Aptoide snapshot has no version list (`nodes.versions.list` is not in it — the same gap that keeps `5.h.v.zo` outside the run), so a history is **first-party only** and a third-party app needs the honest "Not provided" state, which means adding `"version_history"` to `NotProvidedField`; (c) the detail page is a stack of `<section>`s and has no tab widget anywhere, so "tab" is built as a **section**, matching every other block on the page — say so if you wanted a real tabbed UI; (d) `RawVersion.download_url` and `sha256` for older versions exist in the index, but showing them is `5.c.ii.zo` (Held on the contract) and the rollback flow is `5.c.iii.zi`, so **the history shows no download links and no checksums for old versions**. **Recorded design, for the leaves below:** entries keep the index's order (newest first, never re-sorted), each with version name, changelog, size and rollout state; the reader caps the list (pick and record the cap) and counts what it leaves out; a malformed entry is skipped, never thrown on; `release_id` may repeat or be missing, so it is not used as a React key on its own. **Order is deliberate:** reader, then normalizer, then component, then page. `5.c.ii.zo` (older-version links), `5.c.iii.zi` and `5.c.iii.zo` are unaffected and stay separate leaves.

New pure `decideDownload(entry)` returns `{ offered: true, url }` or `{ offered: false, reason }`, `reason` being `pulled`, `halted`, `rolling_out` (rollout not `complete` at 100) or `no_link`, checked in that order. `components/VersionHistory.tsx` and its CSS module: the first entry (the newest release, which the Install button offers and the advisory banner covers) shows neither link nor reason; every later entry shows `Download version <name>` as a plain `<a rel="noopener noreferrer">` or the matching sentence, and one caution line ("Older versions may be missing fixes...") appears once when at least one link is shown. `tests/version-history.test.ts`: the first test updated for the new field, and ten tests added (accepted and rejected URLs, the length limit, the backslash case, every `decideDownload` branch, reader and decision together). **Decisions, recorded, not settled by the operator:** (1) links are withheld for `pulled` and `halted` releases and for a release still rolling out, so a direct link never bypasses a withdrawal or a staged rollout; this is the conservative default and is one line to change in `decideDownload`; (2) no host check on the URL beyond `https://` (the index is signed, and `App.apk` for the newest release is not host-checked either); (3) no checksum or signing fingerprint is shown for an older version. **Flagged, not fixed:** the operator's open call on whether the Install button and download route should refuse a `pulled` newest release is unchanged and untouched; Zealot's download route sends visitors to a login page when a release's channel is password-protected (Cross-repo review item 7), so a link here can lead there; the link is a plain navigation (the `download` attribute is ignored cross-origin), so the browser decides whether it saves or opens the file. **Not done, at the operator's request:** nothing was type-checked, built, tested or run, so the new tests have never executed and the page has not been seen rendered. **5.f — Catalog Database & Platform Risk**

**Requirement — migrations and edge functions live in-repo, not written against a live project:** connecting a real Supabase project to this repo must be a matter of running commands against files already committed here, not a session of writing SQL/function code interactively once a project exists. Concretely:
- Every schema change is a numbered SQL file under `supabase/migrations/` (Supabase CLI's own convention — `supabase migration new <name>` generates the timestamped filename), committed to this repo as part of the leaf that needs it, not applied by hand via the Supabase dashboard. Connecting a project and running `supabase link` + `supabase db push` should replay the entire schema from scratch with no further authoring needed.
- Any server-side logic that needs to run close to the database (webhooks, scheduled jobs, the eventual write-side of `5.g`'s Console read contract, etc.) is a Supabase Edge Function under `supabase/functions/`, committed the same way — `supabase functions deploy` should be the only step, not a first draft written after the project exists.
- This applies retroactively to `5.f.i.zi`/`5.f.i.zo` below: provisioning Supabase and migrating the schema means writing the migration files here first, then pointing the CLI at a real project — not the reverse.
- Local dev/preview never needs a live Supabase project because of this — `supabase start` (the CLI's local Postgres via Docker) can run the exact same committed migrations, matching Phase 0's existing no-live-backend-dependency posture.

**5.g — Developer Console Integration (cross-repo contract)**
*This repo never submits, uploads, authenticates developers, compiles, signs or stores binaries — it only reads the signed catalog index the separate Console (Zealot) publishes and links to the APK the Console holds. These leaves are about the read-side contract, not building the Console itself.*

Wired into `lib/catalog.ts`'s `createZealotSource()`, replacing the mock-`apps` wrapper that function's own comment had already flagged as temporary.

(2) `storage/downloads` writes (both the verified-index cache and the anti-rollback state file) use plain `fs`, which only actually persists between requests where the runtime has persistent local disk — true in dev/this sandbox, **not** true on Vercel per this file's own `5.g.iv.zi` note two lines below. **5.k — Web Push for Saved-App Updates** *(new, split out of `5.c.i.zo` — see that leaf's note. Operator call: true Web Push, subscriptions stored server-side.)*
*Design, as recorded so the leaves below stand alone: the standard model — opt-in on a user gesture, an anonymous per-device subscription (endpoint + keys, no account) stored with the slugs it wants updates for, a server signing with VAPID keys, an event-driven sender, and pruning of expired subscriptions. iOS delivers Web Push only to sites added to the Home Screen (16.4+), so most iPhone visitors are reachable only after installing the PWA. Per-device subscription rows are the one new piece of server-side per-device state in a repo that otherwise keeps favorites/install status/ratings in the browser — `5.k.iv.zo` discloses it. Writes here are the same class as the reviews/reports/counters D-Store already owns in Supabase; the Section 3 rule against live per-request Supabase calls is about catalog/asset reads, not these.*
- 5.k.i — Subscription storage
  - [x] 5.k.i.zi — Supabase migration (`supabase/migrations/`, same posture as the existing six: written and structurally checked, no live Postgres in-sandbox): `push_subscription` (unique `endpoint`, `p256dh`, `auth`, `created_at`, `last_seen_at`; no user id), `push_subscription_app` (subscription FK `on delete cascade`, `slug`), and `push_notified_version` (`slug` primary key, last notified `version`, `notified_at`) — the diff baseline `5.k.iii` reads.

If the database cannot be read (error, missing store, or it does not exist — the worker aborts the open rather than create it) it sends **nothing**, because the subscribe route replaces the whole set and "could not read" must never be sent as "follows nothing"; a genuinely empty list is sent as `[]`. **No rollback on failure**, unlike `enablePush`: nobody is looking at the screen, and keeping the subscription lets `PushSync` re-send the slugs on the next page load (it does whenever a subscription exists). - 5.l.i — Database
  - [x] 5.l.i.zi — Migration: the `catalog_app` table (Supabase, `supabase/migrations/`), with the indexes the paged reads and the search need. Verify in a real PostgreSQL.
    - Done: new `supabase/migrations/20261002000000_create_catalog_app.sql`, the only code-side file; no TypeScript changed, and **nothing reads or writes the table yet**. `public.catalog_app` has one row per Aptoide app: flat columns for what pages filter, sort and search on (`id` `aptoide-<id>`, `slug`, `package_name`, `origin`, `name`, `summary`, `icon`, `version`, `app_type`, `category`, `developer_slug`, `developer_name`, `license`, `size_mb numeric(9,1)`, `download_url`, `reported_downloads bigint`, `is_published`, `source_created_at`, `source_updated_at`, `ingested_at`) plus `raw jsonb`, the source payload as fetched. **Decisions, recorded (the file's header holds the reasoning):** (1) *`raw` is stored, not the normalized `App`,* so a normalizer fix applies to every stored row at once; the null-developer outage (`475f63c`) was fixed that way. The cost: the flat columns are derived at write time and go stale if the mapping changes (a package changes category), until the loader is re-run (not a re-crawl). List reads never select `raw`; the detail page reads it for one slug. (2) *Zealot apps are not rows:* the signed index stays their source and the reader merges them in front; `origin` still allows `'zealot'` so the shape need not change, and nothing writes it. Counters, reviews and reports stay in their own slug-keyed tables with no foreign key to this one. (3) *`slug` and `package_name` are each unique,* so `mergeCatalogSources`'s "first one wins" becomes `on conflict do nothing` in the writer. A `slug` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$` (it becomes a URL segment; all 1,506 snapshot slugs pass), `download_url` is empty or `https://` (the rule `aptoideDownloadUrl` already applies), sizes and counts are not negative. **One row that violates a check fails the whole statement it is in, so the writer must validate against the same slug pattern and count what it skips.** (4) *Indexes,* all plain (none partial): `catalog_app_top_idx` on `(coalesce(reported_downloads,-1) desc, slug)`, `catalog_app_new_idx` on `(source_updated_at desc, slug)`, the same two with `(app_type, category)` in front, `catalog_app_developer_idx`, and two trigram GIN indexes on `name` and `summary` for the existing rule (case-insensitive substring over name or summary). The downloads index is on the *expression* `coalesce(reported_downloads,-1)`, which is the code's `?? -1`, so a cursor is a plain comparison instead of a three-way NULL case; **`5.l.i.zo` must write the identical expression or the planner cannot use it.** (5) *Privileges:* RLS on with no policies, everything revoked from `anon`/`authenticated`, granted to `service_role`, the same posture as `app_counter` and `rate_limit`. (6) *Not included, on purpose:* A-Z order, license, size and region indexes (nothing pages by them; one small migration each when a page does), Aptoide's rating columns (only downloads is used for ordering), and this store's own counters. (7) *Time zone rule:* Aptoide's `added`/`modified` are `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` with no zone; Postgres reads that in the session zone (shown: the same string is `07:46:19` or `14:46:19` UTC depending on the session). **The writer must send an explicit UTC ISO string.** **Verified, in a real PostgreSQL 16.15** (stock Ubuntu package, with `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role` created and Supabase's default grants set, as in earlier sessions): (a) all 19 migrations applied in filename order with `ON_ERROR_STOP`, the new one re-ran clean, it ran as one transaction (`psql -1`, how `scripts/apply-migrations.sh` wraps each file) and it built both trigram indexes with `pg_trgm` already installed in `public`; (b) 42 constraint cases, each refused by the *intended* constraint (duplicate id/slug/package, blank fields, slugs with `/`, `..`, space, newline, leading `-`, empty or non-ASCII, bad origin/type, negative size or downloads, `http:` and `javascript:` URLs, `raw` as an array, string or NULL, a size past `numeric(9,1)`), and the legitimate edges accepted (NULL and 0 downloads, empty URL, the largest real app at 861.1 MB, a column-max size); (c) as `anon` and as `authenticated`, `select`, `insert`, `update`, `delete` and `truncate` are all refused (10 of 10); with a table grant added to `anon` on purpose, RLS still showed 0 rows and blocked the write; as `service_role`, select, insert, update, `on conflict (id) do update`, `on conflict (slug) do nothing`, `on conflict (package_name) do nothing` and delete all work; (d) **all 1,506 real snapshot apps** went through the real `normalizeAptoideApp` (0 failures) and loaded with 0 rejected, under a non-UTC session, with correct UTC timestamps; (e) grown to 10,000 rows (the 1,506 real plus 8,494 copies of real payloads with varied categories, ties, NULL downloads and 87 unpublished), the natural planner used an index for page 1 and keyset pages of the top and new orders, global and per category, for category counts, developer lists, slug and package lookups and the search for a rare or mid-frequency term; "video" chose a sequential scan, and with sequential scans disabled the trigram indexes were used for it (1.5 ms for all matches); (f) a keyset walk of all 9,913 published rows, in pages of 24 and of 1,000, in both orders, returned exactly the full `ORDER BY` sequence with no repeats, over only 28 distinct download values and 566 NULLs; (g) size at 10,000 rows is **71 MB including 15 MB of indexes** (10.4 MB of that is the two trigram indexes); (h) `npx tsc --noEmit` clean and `npm test` 370 of 370 after `npm ci`, which only shows nothing regressed, since no TypeScript changed. **Measured, and it changes the advice:** a cursor written as one `or` (`v < $v or (v = $v and slug > $slug)`) cost 0.1 ms at the start, 1.1 ms at row 3,000 and 4.3 ms at row 9,000; written as two ranges, each with its own `limit`, joined by `union all`, it stayed at about 0.15 ms at every depth. The header tells `5.l.i.zo` to use the two-range form. **Not verified:** (1) **the migration has not been applied to the live Supabase project** (the operator runs `scripts/apply-migrations.sh`; nothing reads the table, so nothing breaks until then, but it must be applied before `5.l.ii.zo`); the `create extension ... with schema extensions` step and the existing `extensions` schema were exercised only on stock Postgres, not on a real Supabase project, and PostgREST's schema cache was not involved. (2) The 10,000-row figures use copies of the 1,506 real payloads, so text-search selectivity and category spread are not real, and the timings are one connection on a sandbox machine with a warm cache, not concurrent load on Supabase's hardware. (3) The scratch scripts (row derivation, load, constraint, privilege, plan and keyset tests) are in `/tmp`, **not committed**; the committed artifact is the migration. **Flagged forward:** (a) *`5.l.i.zo`:* write `coalesce(reported_downloads,-1)` exactly; use the two-range cursor; always filter `is_published`; never select `raw` in a list function; **escape `%`, `_` and `\` in the search needle** (measured: unescaped `w_ats` matched 38 names, escaped matched 0); and, because Supabase exposes functions in `public` over `/rpc` to `anon` by default, revoke `execute` from `public`, `anon` and `authenticated` and grant it to `service_role`, as `5.k.vii.zi` and `check_rate_limit` do. (b) *`5.l.ii.zo` and `5.l.iii.zi`:* derive the flat columns by calling `normalizeAptoideApp`, so they cannot disagree with the detail page; send UTC; validate the slug pattern and report the skip count; use `on conflict (id) do update` for a re-fetch and set `ingested_at = now()` in it. Whether another Aptoide endpoint carries a category was **not checked**. This needs an operator decision or a new leaf (a categorization source) before `5.l.iv.zo`; it does not block `5.l.i.zo` to `5.l.iii.zo`. (d) *Operator:* apply the migration (see Not verified, 1).

(3) `getCatalogScope()` deliberately does not catch a `headers()` failure and fall back to the default tenant: Next signals "render dynamically" by throwing there, and swallowing it would bake the default catalog into a static page. (b) **The Aptoide snapshot is still merged into every tenant's catalog** behind its own Zealot index; it has no tenant concept, and whether a white-label tenant should carry it is a product call. (c) **No build-time snapshot or per-file SHA-256 verification (`5.g.iv.zi`) for non-default tenants:** the prebuild script only snapshots the default index, so a non-default tenant relies on the live fetch plus a best-effort disk cache (which may not persist on a read-only serverless filesystem). (e) The per-scope memo is per process lifetime with no TTL, and a failed first resolution is memoized as empty until restart, both unchanged from before, now per tenant. (f) If a tenant's `catalog_index_base_url` changes, the fallback cache is still that tenant's file from the old URL, since the cache holds no record of which URL produced it.

## 3. Standing Handoff Process (mandatory, every session)

This is the same process used to hand off the D-Store documentation itself — it is now the fixed rule for every session, no exceptions.

**Key location — cache files:** the storefront reads catalog/asset data from local cache files only, never live per-request calls to Supabase or the Console (Zealot) — this keeps the app populated and responsive even if either upstream is briefly unreachable. Cached/downloaded files live at **`storage/downloads`**. Any leaf that touches caching, downloads, or catalog population must read from and write to this location; note it explicitly in the commit body when a leaf adds or changes what's cached there.

0. **Cross-repo run:** clone the other repos and read their handovers first (see "Cross-repo run — standing rules" in Section 0), then **check upstream:** `git fetch origin` and compare against `origin/master`. If origin has moved since the local clone/session was last synced (earlier patches already applied and pushed, for instance), rebase local work onto the current `origin/master` (`git rebase origin/master`) before starting the leaf and before generating any patch. A patch built against a stale base will fail to apply with `git am` even when the content it wants is logically identical to what's already there — this step is what prevents that.
1. **Do the one assigned leaf task** (Section 1 — nothing more).
2. **Update this file**: flip the completed leaf's `[ ]` to `[x]`, append one line for the leaf to `CHANGELOG.md` (`leaf path — short title`, no hash: a commit cannot know its own; see that file's header), and move the "Current position" line (Section 0) to the next open leaf in path order (`zi` before `zo`; within a milestone before moving to the next `i/ii/iii`; within a track before the next `a/b/c/d`; within a phase before the next `1/2/3/4`).
2a. **Refresh the "START HERE" block at the top of this file** (rewrite it, do not append): the leaf the program is on and its state, the `N done ✅ of M` count, what is done, pending or blocked and **on whom**, the repo head commits and any patch not yet applied, and the exact first command or step for the next session. A session that leaves it stale has not finished, because the block is the only part of this file a new session is told to trust without reading further. Lasting facts do not stay in it: move them to the section they belong to (a Render or CI fact to "CI and deploy debugging", a decision to the leaf's Done note).
3. **Commit** the code change and the `HANDOVER.md` update **together**, in one commit, with a message that starts with the leaf path:
   ```
   git add -A
   git commit -m "1.a.i.zi: add install_count, avg_rating, rating_count fields"
   ```
4. **Generate the patch**, based on the current `origin/master` (from step 0), for that single commit:
   ```
   git format-patch -1 HEAD -o patches/
   ```
5. **Hand the patch file to the user** — never push directly unless explicitly told to. The patch is the deliverable that closes the session. **Always hand off exactly one patch file, never more than one.** If a handoff spans several commits (e.g. a multi-commit resequencing session, or several small fixes batched together), combine them into a single file with `git format-patch origin/master --stdout > patches/000X-<description>.patch` — this produces one mbox-style file containing all the commits since the real upstream state, in order, which `git am` applies in one shot. Do not hand off several separate `.patch` files for one handoff.
6. The next session applies it with:
   ```
   cd ~/D-Store
   git am ~/storage/downloads/000X-<leaf-path>-<description>.patch
   git push origin master
   ```

7. **If a CI run or a deploy failed** (this session's or one the operator mentions), the standing rule in Section 0, "CI and deploy debugging", comes first: hand over the log command (`scripts/fetch-ci-log.sh`), saved under `~/storage/downloads`, and read the uploaded file before fixing anything.

**Focus-run reporting (only while the "Focus run" checklist in Section 0 is active):** after step 6's hand-off, end the final message with `N done ✅` as defined there. The checklist tick, the count and Current position are updated in the leaf's own commit (step 2), so the patch and the count can never disagree.

If a leaf can't be finished in one session, do not commit partial work as done — mark it `[~]`, commit what exists with a `WIP:` prefix, note in the commit body exactly what's left, and still hand off a patch. The next session resumes that same leaf before touching "Current position."

*This file is the single source of truth for what to work on. If it disagrees with any other document, HANDOVER.md wins for sequencing; D-STORE.md wins for feature/design specification.*
